trust_decision.summary: Prototype pollution is decided at the key-copy step of _.merge: a key from the source object is used as a property name with no filter, and because an own '__proto__' key from JSON.parse shadows the accessor, the recursion is handed Object.prototype as its target. The published fix blocks three key names at that one step.

landing_point.why: the only _.merge definition in the tree, named directly in the advisory summary; the fix hunk header (fix.diff:9) points here

fix_sites.entry_point: _.merge, public export of @feathersjs/commons (import { _ } from '@feathersjs/commons'); no in-repo caller exists, only tests

O3_reason_to_dismiss: _.extend/_.omit/_.pick only set the prototype of the object they build and can never reach Object.prototype, and pick/omit are load-bearing on record data (packages/knex/src/adapter.ts:287, packages/mongodb/src/adapter.ts:209), so a solver can argue the advisory's global-pollution property does not cover them.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: In-place recursive merge into an existing target must keep working (nested keys merged, target object mutated and returned), and non-object arguments must pass through unchanged (_.merge('hello', {}) === 'hello'); a fix that swaps the recursion for Object.assign/spread, deep-clones, or rejects any source containing the three names breaks the documented contract.

O6_input_shapes: the same payload at any recursion depth (guard runs per level)
deeply nested plain objects and non-object sources, which must keep merging/returning unchanged

O8_uncovered_routes.route: select() passes client-controlled params.query.$select field names into _.pick, which copies each key into a fresh object with no key filter; a record holding an own '__proto__' key from the adapter's JSON round-trip then sets the returned record's prototype.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names _.merge; _.pick only rewrites the prototype of the object it returns, never Object.prototype, so it is a different, non-global issue.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: _.extend is Object.assign(first, ...rest) with no key filter, and _.omit builds its result through it, so a JSON-parsed '__proto__' key sets the prototype of the object handed back to the caller.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Object.assign can only change the target's own prototype, never Object.prototype, so it is not the global pollution the advisory describes.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~20 lines above the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a _.defaults / _.deepCopy / _.set helper built on the same _.extend/Object.assign key copy
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the _ object is explicitly a hand-rolled lodash replacement (packages/commons/src/index.ts:8), so adding another lodash-y copy helper into the same bag is in character for the maintainers

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a deep merge of environment config into app settings instead of the current shallow spread
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: config loading is the classic place a maintainer would want defaults deep-merged, and the file already copies every config key onto the app

O8b_injection_room.sibling: nested $select projection that would merge/copy selected field paths into a result object
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: select() already maps a client-supplied key list through _.pick; adding nested projection is a natural extension request

O9_family: prototype pollution (CWE-1321) via prototype-key inheritance in a recursive object merge

O10_build.toolchain: npm workspaces + lerna; tsc compile per package; mocha + ts-node via .mocharc.json
O10_build.project_tests: packages/commons/test/utils.test.ts — mocha 'merge' describe block (lines 169-214); package script mocha --config ../../.mocharc.json

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Skip only the '__proto__' string in _.merge for the single JSON shape in the report, validate through _.merge itself, and stop.
